strings.title: Play WuWa in VR
strings.subtitle: {version} player guide · Wuthering Waves {game} · Windows PCVR
strings.intro: Install WuWa-VR-Setup.exe, then open the WuWa VR shortcut. No separate Python installation is needed. The first VR-package installation needs internet; the small Setup download contains the launcher app.
strings.step1.title: 01 · Choose your game
strings.step1.body: Check the detected or saved location. Use Change to select Steam or the official Kuro launcher. If browsing for Steam, choose its Wuthering Waves.exe, not the inner Shipping executable. Choose explicitly if you have several installations.
strings.step2.title: 02 · Install WuWa VR
strings.step2.body: Check the target game version, read the account-risk notice and select Install VR. The package is verified before installation. Installing does not start the game.
strings.step2.parts: Launcher app is this desktop window. VR package is the mod and its tools. Updating one does not automatically update the other.
strings.step3.title: 03 · Choose the runtime, then launch
strings.step3.runtime: Start your headset software and select Use headset, or choose Use bundled simulator for a desktop preview. Launch needs a working headset runtime, or the simulator that belongs to the selected VR package.
strings.step3.changes: Runtime changes are explicit, may ask for Windows permission and need WuWa and its injector to be closed. Opening, installing or updating the launcher never changes the runtime by itself.
strings.step3.launch: Select Launch in VR and accept Windows permission when asked. Steam starts the game through Steam; with Kuro, press Play in its launcher. Your choices are remembered.
strings.notice: Unofficial community mod, not approved by Kuro Games. Injection may trigger anti-cheat or account restrictions. Review and accept the notice before proceeding.
strings.updates.title: Updates and rollback
strings.updates.check: When a new version of the app is available, a bar at the top offers it: update, then use Restart to update when idle. When the app starts, it installs a newer VR package for the same game version by itself while the game is closed; the package you had stays installed. Troubleshooting → Versions & updates lists every published version and has Check for updates. A failed update check or a cached list does not mean your package is current.
strings.updates.release: This release pairs app {version} with package {tag}, for WuWa {game}. To undo a VR-package update, close the game and injector, stop recording, then use Back to … in step 02. This does not roll back the launcher app. Settings, backups and recordings are kept.
strings.updates.blocked: If app updating is blocked, use the latest Setup from the website. Reinstalling does not stop a stuck background worker; use the recovery steps below first.
strings.portable.body: Download WuWa-VR-Launcher.zip from the matching release, extract everything and open WuWa VR Launcher.exe. Keep its folders together. This opens the separate web tool interface; it does not update the installed desktop app.
strings.controls.title: Everyday controls
strings.controls.intro: Xbox / XInput is the usual gameplay path. L3 / R3 mean click the left / right stick. Not sure? Hold L3, or LT + RT, for half a second: a card rises under your view and shows what each button does, lighting each one as you press it. Release controls between shortcuts. Insert opens the menu with the keyboard.
strings.controls.cards.input: Hold L3, or LT + RT, for half a second
strings.controls.cards.action: A card with the buttons for that hold. Let go and it sinks away. The L3 card starts pinned, low in front of you; L3 + Menu hides it or pins it again.
strings.controls.menu.action: Open or close the WuWa VR menu: point with a VR controller's laser and pull the trigger, or use A / B and LB / RB. UEVR's full settings: Menu → All settings (classic UEVR menu).
strings.controls.next.input: Hold both LT + RT first, then click R3
strings.controls.next.action: Switch between full VR and the stereo screen; keep the triggers held to click R3 again
strings.controls.full.input: Hold both LT + RT first, then hold R3 for 0.8 seconds
strings.controls.full.action: Mono theatre on or off (the same flat picture in both eyes; easy on the eyes in menus and cutscenes); hold again to go back to the view you had
strings.controls.blur.input: Hold both LT + RT first, then click L3
strings.controls.blur.action: Blur (depth of field) on or off; on by default, in both eyes
strings.controls.portal.input: Hold L3, then fully squeeze LT / RT
strings.controls.portal.action: Portal window / temporary 10× diorama. Keep the other trigger released. F7 also toggles the portal.
strings.controls.recenter.action: Recenter view / show or hide game UI
strings.controls.camera.action: First person / game or fixed camera
strings.controls.playstation: PS4 / PS5: Steam Input or another working Xbox / XInput mapping uses the same shortcuts. Cross / Circle / Square / Triangle are A / B / X / Y, L1 / R1 are LB / RB, L2 / R2 are LT / RT, Share / Create is View and Options is Menu. Experimental direct DualShock 4 and DualSense input also works when no XInput pad is active, but the game may react to the same buttons. See the full reference.
strings.controls.views: The WuWa VR menu's Cinema page has the view, blur and close-up options. Automatic switching for cutscenes is experimental and off; keep the manual view shortcut handy.
strings.optional.summary: Optional walking with VR controllers, diorama and hand demo
strings.optional.walk: VR controllers (Quick page) let Quest controllers act as an Xbox pad for walking and sightseeing. They start off each launch. Hold the left Menu button for 1 second to turn them on or off (a buzz confirms); a quick press is still Start. Without a Menu button (Index), hold both stick clicks for 1 second while they are off. With VR controllers the cards name the grips, triggers and sticks.
strings.optional.share: Sharing with Xbox / treadmill is remembered: Both together (default; treadmill walking keeps working), Last used wins, or VR only. Controller slot is Automatic by default: it uses the slot that has a controller, such as Reality Runner's virtual pad. Both are on the WuWa VR menu's Controllers page, with Treadmill run: while Reality Runner is open, walking starts a run that times you and saves your route in the game. See the walking reference.
strings.optional.diorama: Diorama needs Native Stereo and enlarges head movement with the world scale; turning it off restores your normal scale. The hand / finger demo is a visualization only, without grabbing or gestures.
strings.recovery.title: If something goes wrong
strings.recovery.stuck: Startup stuck: use Stop waiting and allow up to four seconds. If cancellation is not confirmed, open Troubleshooting → Stuck launcher processes → Find stuck launcher processes, select only the worker you mean to stop, then confirm Stop selected. Nothing is preselected. Then choose Retry connection.
strings.recovery.close: Cannot close: Close launcher only closes the window and leaves background work alone. Recovery never stops WuWa, Steam, the injector or a VR runtime.
strings.recovery.controller: Controller missing: Controller check reads XInput slots and HidHide information without changing settings. A connected slot does not prove the game receives the buttons.
strings.recovery.hud: Squashed HUD: open and close ESC; the WuWa VR menu's HUD page also has Refresh HUD layout. L3 + B shows hidden game UI again.
strings.recovery.report: Report a problem: on the WuWa VR menu's Record page, pick what went wrong and choose Save report; in the launcher use Copy diagnostics and Report an issue. Include the app and VR-package versions, what happened and a recording if you have one.
strings.uninstall.body: Troubleshooting → Prepare uninstall removes verified downloads after you confirm, when idle; then uninstall the app in Windows Settings → Apps. The game, settings, backups, recordings, the active OpenXR package and busy or unverified files are kept. Reinstalling does not stop a stuck background worker.
strings.recording.title: Recording and current limits
strings.recording.body: Start and stop recording from the WuWa VR menu (Record video) or from Developer tools in the launcher's footer. Recording supports SteamVR and the bundled simulator; it does not support VDXR or audio. Player IDs are covered while it records. Check videos for names and account details before sharing. See the feedback guide.
strings.recording.limits: What was tested for this release, and the known limits, are in the release notes. Known issues include long scene or dialogue stalls, a HUD that can stay squashed until ESC, moving flat-menu backgrounds and close-ups that are sometimes wider than in 2D. Mono theatre helps with some menus and cutscenes.
